citation: Kelly, Hart & Rose, J. Phys. Energy 3 (2021)

capture_scheme: pion production in W target; muons from pi- decay
derivation: as-published; no OURS-normalization (already GeV per muon). Optimized G4Beamline point: Kelly Sec.5 item (a) -- a lettered item in his running text, introduced by 'In the table, it is worth noting:', NOT a footnote to the table -- divides his Table 1 beam energy by the 0.77 negative muons per beam particle and quotes 4.70 GeV/muon; the printed digits give 3606/0.77 = 4683 MeV = 4.68 GeV, so 4.70 is his quoted figure carried as published and the 0.4% is his rounding, not ours (deuteron on W; 150 fusions/muon). source_locator: DOI 10.1088/2515-7655/abfb4b (open access); 4.70 GeV/muon: his Sec.5 item (a), the lettered item in the running text introduced by 'In the table, it is worth noting:'; Q_elec=14% at X_mu=150: his sec.6
notes: THE open-access anchor (G4Beamline, fully checkable). eta_acc=0.18 (PSI-measured; verified against the published text: in his sec.7 the sentence after the one naming the right-hand chart of figure 3 reads '(150 fusions per muon, 18% accelerator efficiency)'. His sec.6 also discusses figure 3, and the sentence after that reference says something else -- 'At our current assumed level of 150 fusion reactions per muon, we obtain Qelec = 14%' -- so the two must not be conflated); Q_elec=14% at X_mu=150 (that pairing is the sec.6 sentence quoted above; his abstract states the 14% without the 150-fusion condition); recapture credit x2.5 in recapture_factor, NOT folded into 4.70. Locator: his ABSTRACT states the cost 'can be reduced by a factor of 2.5 below current values' and that 'This is done by recapturing the kinetic energy of waste particles and generating heat through tritium breeding'. Two nearest counterexamples, both disclosed rather than resolved: his Sec.7 attaches 'the improvement in Q by a factor of ~2.5' to a different quantity, and the recovery step he actually prints for the optimized configuration is Q=0.83 (Sec.5 item (a), fusion heat only: 26.0 MeV/fusion x150 = 3.9 GeV) against Q=1.87 (Table 1 caption, Q=F/G) -- a ratio the paper never names as a factor. eta_mu (basis record): Kelly Sec.6 defines eta_mu as '(c) failure to deliver negative muons to dt vessels' and then states VERBATIM: 'we do not know eta_mu and finding it will be the focus of phase three of our research. For the current phase we will use the arbitrary but reasonable assumption of eta_mu = 50%'. That factor is the whole capture+transport+moderate+stop segment collapsed into one number, and its own authors call it arbitrary -- so it is recorded (eta_mu_assumption=0.50, eta_mu_evidence_status=author_declared_arbitrary), NEVER folded into normalized_GeV_per_mu, and any figure composing it is a BOUND that may not headline.

derivation: as-published beam-energy-per-muon at liquid density rho_0 (Table II, n-beam 3.5 GeV/c: C_mu = 7.8 +- 1.8 GeV); no OURS-normalization. Full design-study span: ~3 GeV ideal (all muons collected, intermediate beam) to ~8-10 GeV (liquid in-target: n 7.8, p 10.0, d 8.8 GeV).
source_locator: Table II p.879, C_mu- column at target density rho_0, n beam 3.5 GeV/c; C_pi- definition p.876; in-flight pi- decay probability W p.878 with fig.3 p.879; Conclusions p.880 (iii ~8 GeV liquid in-target; iv ~3 GeV ideal all-collected)
notes: Full-text-verified from the primary PDF on 2026-07-11 and re-read from the rendered pages on 2026-08-29 (DOI 10.1209/0295-5075/4/8/003). Costs fall at sub-liquid density (0.5/0.2/0.1 rho_0 -> 4.3/2.6/2.0 GeV n-beam) but muCF needs liquid density. The paper notes agreement with Jandel et al. (CERN-TH 4703/87). RE-TYPED 2026-08-29 from stage stopped_useful_in_dt / basis_class stopped_in_dt to produced: Table II is captioned as the cost of PRODUCING muons, C_mu- is built from the beam energy per negative pion and the probability that such a pion decays in flight inside the target, and nothing about the muon after its birth -- range, escape, collection, stopping -- is computed anywhere in pp.875-880. Where the Conclusions do reach for the fate of the muons (iv), it is to say that the cost of the ALTERNATIVE intermediate-beam approach depends on their canalization, which they do not quantify either. The muon is counted at birth inside the fuel, so this figure is a LOWER BOUND on the cost per muon stopped and useful in D-T, exactly like the other PINNED rows of its tier (jandel_1989 carries no figure, so it is not a bound either way). needs_verification stays false and is not a comment on that re-typing: the flag records whether the DIGIT is pinned from the primary text, and 7.8 +- 1.8 GeV is pinned from Table II. Two details a reader checking the locator will meet: the Table II caption prints C_pi- where the table's own column head over those figures and the sentence introducing it both read C_mu-, evidently a misprint; and the FLUKA86/87 code of ref. 8 is the PION-production Monte Carlo -- the pion-muon conversion was computed analytically and cross-checked against a Monte Carlo calculation that p.878 says, in the passive, was also developed.
